sections.title: Sound of the letter é
paragraphs: The letter (é) /e/ is called (é) /e/. Its most common spoken sound appears in the word (escola) /iʃˈkɔ.lɐ/, which means school. This letter can make four different vowel sounds in Portuguese.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, keep your mouth almost closed and pull your tongue back. For the second sound, spread your lips wide and raise your tongue high. For the third sound, raise the middle of your tongue slightly and relax your lips. For the fourth sound, drop your jaw lower and open your mouth wide. Place your hand on your throat to feel your voice buzz throughout all four sounds.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: In an unstressed syllable or at the end of a word, it sounds like /ɨ/, as in (de) /dɨ/. At the beginning of a word before the letters s or x and a consonant, it makes the sound /i/, as in (estar) /iʃˈtaɾ/. In a stressed closed syllable, it makes the sound /e/, as in (mesa) /ˈme.zɐ/. In a stressed open syllable or with an acute accent, it sounds like /ɛ/, as in (café) /kɐˈfɛ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not pronounce the sound /ɨ/ like the vowel in the English word roses. Keep your mouth nearly shut and swallow the sound slightly instead. Do not say the sound /e/ like the vowel glide in day. Keep your tongue completely still so the vowel does not slide at the end.
